GameRequest.title: GameRequest
GameRequest.description: Represents a request for a game made by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the game request.

gameName.description: The name of the game being requested.

platform.description: The platform for which the game is being requested (PC, PS4/5, Xbox, Switch).

name.description: The name of the user submitting the request.

email.description: The email of the user submitting the request.

notes.description: Additional notes or comments provided by the user.

requestDate.description: The date and time when the game request was submitted.

AvailableGame.title: AvailableGame
AvailableGame.description: Represents a game that is available on the platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the available game.

name.description: The name of the available game.

supportedPlatforms.description: An array of platforms on which the game is supported.

imageUrl.description: URL of the image representing the game.

UserAccount.title: UserAccount
UserAccount.description: Represents a user account on the platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account.

creationDate.description: The date and time when the user account was created.

UserMessage.title: UserMessage
UserMessage.description: Represents a message sent or received by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user message.

senderId.description: Reference to UserAccount. The ID of the user who sent the message. (Relationship: UserAccount 1:N UserMessage)

receiverId.description: Reference to UserAccount. The ID of the user who received the message. (Relationship: UserAccount 1:N UserMessage)

timestamp.description: The date and time when the message was sent.

isRead.description: Indicates whether the message has been read by the recipient.

params.name: gameRequestId

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support the RAFA Project Launcher application, focusing on game requests, available games, user accounts, and user messages. The key principle is Authorization Independence, achieved through denormalization where necessary.  The structure uses structural segregation to maintain a homogeneous security posture within collections.

*   **Game Requests:** Stored in a dedicated collection (`game_requests`). No user-specific access control is required for reading these (admin review only). However, including the user's ID with each request can facilitate future features like request history.
*   **Available Games:** Stored in a dedicated collection (`available_games`). These are globally available and don't require specific access controls.
*   **User Accounts:** Stored in a user-specific collection (`users/{userId}`). This ensures that user data is private and only accessible by the user themselves.
*   **User Messages:**  Utilizes a subcollection under each user (`users/{userId}/messages/{messageId}`). This provides path-based ownership, making it very secure and efficient to implement security rules. It also enables secure list operations (QAPs) as only the user can access their messages.

This design prioritizes clarity and debuggability by avoiding complex hierarchical authorization dependencies. Each data collection is designed to have clear ownership and purpose, simplifying the implementation of security rules.
